q: Enoch AI dating Dead Sea Scrolls
transcript:
Researchers at the University of Groningen developed an artificial intelligence model named [Enoch](https://www.google.com/search?q=Enoch) to re-date the [Dead Sea Scrolls](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fg%2F121sxbzn&q=Dead+Sea+Scrolls). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHrOzAVVCGjY0RA8b53QRhKrDyt2cLac43m-P9TQ97bgLJz_b70_5P-ZKJDmDE4gIEiW0Ua5Xur6czznOEKrb5LVCgYvtJsAKjKx5h99H9VJMcKSFR_b1Daotkr9ZbZcSrT4MGGzmmm)]
How Enoch Works
   * Training Data: The model was trained on 24 radiocarbon-dated scroll samples from four Judean Desert sites. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESpwEB6zswFcBZcmVZs2oOAHirsFqcGYSaxV1VpG6K9ZCUdjUJEw-EEMJLm7rZYtV1lv_LkWw1xw4tUD2Z6Tc7fEPiWhuByBScdQpVTfuBuRqBvXQtppGz1Jk8VEK8DGUbqfTKliMzSEQxd9hhaVPG5-SLJn8j_XWTTklfMIbmi6_psy2KPg8YD7cxDObnGjDESTtoiEgoPdJ17Xqr45Z4cRl4FZAmNbmHVw), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESagHrOzAVduU7-HR8DFr0K4W6ZI9ZP3POUxc_-GUwLiozJ4T8RG4iGSuvc97rMD5LsRdxCta6_U2vA7kysWqPbRZPHK5xH1BUWBQzm0S5HQson8VTytszfCFpk4nW8CkpPXsixojHl4faGvM)]
   * Methodology: It combines Bayesian ridge regression, radiocarbon dating, and machine-learning handwriting analysis (evaluating angular and allographic stroke geometries from manuscript images without reading the text itself). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEB6zswFTLgpOEe42rLGhAY_ihwls3dwVZqVKJC4ojHSMIj97soRVNkK6A9bpt4AhxcecYFI-hwp6Cw2pHTF1b2SXyl5vNbtGEq8L-X7OcFaWDbGWgCwKXODTEc22PX4NXidfIVLl4XXEkiCS0rntvy5WG4U9q-FVm9ewKjeGBcWF8), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHrOzAV7XK-KwOL33JCSxZQq4dTQ-Tq463rpU0-xSedeyPG1F3kvArZhTk6IG06190G74J6aA0wizdeeNLGNU-9W6Ei2vT5W-ONw48uBPb41-nLHhjuI4jvZ6tnLwt0wjmtRg)]
   * Accuracy: Enoch predicts dates with a mean absolute error of roughly 28 to 31 years, and 79% of its estimates for 135 undated scrolls aligned realistically with human paleographic evaluations. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAES2QEB6zswFeSBxaD4RVuTUGo-tpMbFqkcWEZV8_0Bjpaa3DxXXVLeUnOoh1yK23IsrAMC7gJAICaOyhyi_7e3fzOqF7uiCcSTpSmsdiZBcxiD8RgM-8uutlBpgkB7ef4DF3tjnsLSboxT2lEup2I3zvmMJZH6iCeBMGQBlalByADn308x6SkjedmE7avTGX4o-xgpIVDvmW3XTVUE0ZfFoBLRjVi2A1LDcEB5b8L2wiimFIMTpL1aDEBMBpn0h8Rax5BaryTiRHLz1VHbDLJO1nd5CqioBdhPUxPk), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEB6zswFTLgpOEe42rLGhAY_ihwls3dwVZqVKJC4ojHSMIj97soRVNkK6A9bpt4AhxcecYFI-hwp6Cw2pHTF1b2SXyl5vNbtGEq8L-X7OcFaWDbGWgCwKXODTEc22PX4NXidfIVLl4XXEkiCS0rntvy5WG4U9q-FVm9ewKjeGBcWF8), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESagHrOzAVduU7-HR8DFr0K4W6ZI9ZP3POUxc_-GUwLiozJ4T8RG4iGSuvc97rMD5LsRdxCta6_U2vA7kysWqPbRZPHK5xH1BUWBQzm0S5HQson8VTytszfCFpk4nW8CkpPXsixojHl4faGvM)]
Key Findings
   * Older Timelines: Enoch indicates that a significant portion of the scrolls are 50 to 150 years older than traditional paleographic estimates. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHrOzAVVCGjY0RA8b53QRhKrDyt2cLac43m-P9TQ97bgLJz_b70_5P-ZKJDmDE4gIEiW0Ua5Xur6czznOEKrb5LVCgYvtJsAKjKx5h99H9VJMcKSFR_b1Daotkr9ZbZcSrT4MGGzmmm)]
   * Specific Texts:
      * The Daniel fragment (`4Q114`) and Ecclesiastes manuscript (`4Q109`) were backdated substantially—with Ecclesiastes potentially pushed back from 175–150 BCE to roughly 300–250 BCE.
      * Some copies appear closer in time to their presumed historical authors or predate major periods like the Hasmonean kingdom expansion and the Qumran settlement. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESwwEB6zswFTgqvHyiuPUYKb3jfB9s6lEQYwTYix0POLVAnUWuWm6yVtgjtciV98Y2Vdw6s9kOOofSHoX2xj2S_Q1H1Q9GlXvqKiM6uUWNjijD4NoXUkzY-nl2oLm2T9QBLoHEiJnXCsp00F83BilQE0Wv5MSzl796EBVUkeCg51X2rOzzEaMAZZtV13-i_s9_sKXxWCyp8mUn0DLHRxYDZdEqZ3yBasa-1PBZ4BCtziFAvTrwcGf_XSvaPotyBwiz1dW7LP4), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHrOzAVVCGjY0RA8b53QRhKrDyt2cLac43m-P9TQ97bgLJz_b70_5P-ZKJDmDE4gIEiW0Ua5Xur6czznOEKrb5LVCgYvtJsAKjKx5h99H9VJMcKSFR_b1Daotkr9ZbZcSrT4MGGzmmm), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEB6zswFTLgpOEe42rLGhAY_ihwls3dwVZqVKJC4ojHSMIj97soRVNkK6A9bpt4AhxcecYFI-hwp6Cw2pHTF1b2SXyl5vNbtGEq8L-X7OcFaWDbGWgCwKXODTEc22PX4NXidfIVLl4XXEkiCS0rntvy5WG4U9q-FVm9ewKjeGBcWF8)]
Scholarly and Community Reaction
   * Support: Supporters view Enoch as an objective "time machine" that injects quantifiable error margins into handwriting analysis.
   * Skepticism: On platforms like [Reddit](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESqAEB6zswFUSI1o9h3UO3PlMOLJtiZcSIGt6bjfIEXpeE2WENSYUxnqNQKM9qb_dj0GigjAYBWw8MAcGhmMQeqElwazQOsf3Hjtcfp6Y1I4-u5VC87N59p8-xTQASf7TVc3sN2KvkKdTw7tAyQnJ3HZJeceKZdbTcItMkZEuetZBTDl3Ks5_4dhLgqv8aGzEnQSgXRWn_2GRiJalt5D4r2UMiNiLD4ep4b48), opinions are mixed, with some researchers and users raising caution over black-box AI models, carbon-dating uncertainties, and traditional historical assumptions. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESqAEB6zswFUSI1o9h3UO3PlMOLJtiZcSIGt6bjfIEXpeE2WENSYUxnqNQKM9qb_dj0GigjAYBWw8MAcGhmMQeqElwazQOsf3Hjtcfp6Y1I4-u5VC87N59p8-xTQASf7TVc3sN2KvkKdTw7tAyQnJ3HZJeceKZdbTcItMkZEuetZBTDl3Ks5_4dhLgqv8aGzEnQSgXRWn_2GRiJalt5D4r2UMiNiLD4ep4b48), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHrOzAV7XK-KwOL33JCSxZQq4dTQ-Tq463rpU0-xSedeyPG1F3kvArZhTk6IG06190G74J6aA0wizdeeNLGNU-9W6Ei2vT5W-ONw48uBPb41-nLHhjuI4jvZ6tnLwt0wjmtRg), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHrOzAVeoPYFwJc-yeghu_3T7aJ-xf1ylKNwIQt6cCGahQWdTutiIm_bo3pgxX3JYohWNizYzQjpKli8_8sD5liPiKNTKk_5obuiA23_xLswRuq5Em3gXt2bkvBCoqtlTnh1pgXoxj9Og)]
Opinions on the reliability and implications of AI-driven dating for ancient manuscripts vary among researchers and the public.
“More research is needed to understand how Enoch's work will affect our understanding of the chronology of the Dead Sea Scrolls, Popovic cautions.”
[Haaretz](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAES2QEB6zswFeSBxaD4RVuTUGo-tpMbFqkcWEZV8_0Bjpaa3DxXXVLeUnOoh1yK23IsrAMC7gJAICaOyhyi_7e3fzOqF7uiCcSTpSmsdiZBcxiD8RgM-8uutlBpgkB7ef4DF3tjnsLSboxT2lEup2I3zvmMJZH6iCeBMGQBlalByADn308x6SkjedmE7avTGX4o-xgpIVDvmW3XTVUE0ZfFoBLRjVi2A1LDcEB5b8L2wiimFIMTpL1aDEBMBpn0h8Rax5BaryTiRHLz1VHbDLJO1nd5CqioBdhPUxPk)

Ithaca is a deep neural network developed by Google DeepMind and academic partners to restore, geographically attribute, and chronologically date damaged ancient Greek inscriptions. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYQHrOzAV9bhPXwiPFAkk0WrtjwF69osLlHBUWNzzI69S1WtwZTqUCsUsFHJRmbHqvOTqawUMo9x8Q-JEjDS2uEGe-nwFB8K7bhK_9tMlb9RUSeY2GDejKtZrzQPcaK1YQ8A)]
Key Capabilities
   * Text Restoration: Restores missing or damaged characters with 62% accuracy on its own (raising human historian accuracy from 25% to 72% when collaborating). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYQHrOzAV9bhPXwiPFAkk0WrtjwF69osLlHBUWNzzI69S1WtwZTqUCsUsFHJRmbHqvOTqawUMo9x8Q-JEjDS2uEGe-nwFB8K7bhK_9tMlb9RUSeY2GDejKtZrzQPcaK1YQ8A)]
   * Geographical Attribution: Identifies the original geographic location across 84 regions with 71% accuracy. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHrOzAV_0MWkpVTpN7uvNvXlOBaZ40iii-iOTMqzp09h7b0HxKyB-_B3anpWxAEboASgFYZPv2f1wL6NWVEbFQlf4ki9DS6MGXMox5jtuJ6YxNutsIntryMo_rhg8_NQ3HN7Mpl7kEKmaM9FC0kvaP9Eb726w), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESagHrOzAVvUud25tCo9gLWQgmo4vGXjLWeVFxE5AU0Uki3Gg-oMDVXRFMODGH1hrVZkipV_2rQt9md-GkhXBTCM2McqHlXUfunJiUdmKCar8LAG0D4xDoHA6uzaN6yPDhb_m-D2SdWYGdhSk)]
   * Chronological Dating: Dates inscriptions within 30 years of their true historical creation date. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHrOzAV_0MWkpVTpN7uvNvXlOBaZ40iii-iOTMqzp09h7b0HxKyB-_B3anpWxAEboASgFYZPv2f1wL6NWVEbFQlf4ki9DS6MGXMox5jtuJ6YxNutsIntryMo_rhg8_NQ3HN7Mpl7kEKmaM9FC0kvaP9Eb726w)]
How It Works
   * Architecture: Uses joint character and word embeddings with stacked transformer decoder blocks and sparse multi-head attention. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESagHrOzAVvUud25tCo9gLWQgmo4vGXjLWeVFxE5AU0Uki3Gg-oMDVXRFMODGH1hrVZkipV_2rQt9md-GkhXBTCM2McqHlXUfunJiUdmKCar8LAG0D4xDoHA6uzaN6yPDhb_m-D2SdWYGdhSk), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHrOzAV_0MWkpVTpN7uvNvXlOBaZ40iii-iOTMqzp09h7b0HxKyB-_B3anpWxAEboASgFYZPv2f1wL6NWVEbFQlf4ki9DS6MGXMox5jtuJ6YxNutsIntryMo_rhg8_NQ3HN7Mpl7kEKmaM9FC0kvaP9Eb726w)]
   * Training Data: Trained on the Packard Humanities Institute (PHI) Searchable Greek Inscriptions dataset. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHrOzAV_0MWkpVTpN7uvNvXlOBaZ40iii-iOTMqzp09h7b0HxKyB-_B3anpWxAEboASgFYZPv2f1wL6NWVEbFQlf4ki9DS6MGXMox5jtuJ6YxNutsIntryMo_rhg8_NQ3HN7Mpl7kEKmaM9FC0kvaP9Eb726w), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYQHrOzAV9bhPXwiPFAkk0WrtjwF69osLlHBUWNzzI69S1WtwZTqUCsUsFHJRmbHqvOTqawUMo9x8Q-JEjDS2uEGe-nwFB8K7bhK_9tMlb9RUSeY2GDejKtZrzQPcaK1YQ8A)]
   * Access & Open Source: The code is open-sourced under the Apache-2.0 license via the [GitHub - Google-DeepMind Ithaca Repository](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYQHrOzAV9bhPXwiPFAkk0WrtjwF69osLlHBUWNzzI69S1WtwZTqUCsUsFHJRmbHqvOTqawUMo9x8Q-JEjDS2uEGe-nwFB8K7bhK_9tMlb9RUSeY2GDejKtZrzQPcaK1YQ8A), and interactive research tools can be explored through [Predicting the Past](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVgHrOzAV5xjfiCSPWOfGgOXOl09A2Ia9t8w6n3GOcZKu8sNgrR6XHIbDPTs6hdVLhRmsBR_nK-WQVer7zY6gPSmm1pIQT5soqR4Dqyo3prIvXmk6EpMN). [Aeneas](https://www.google.com/search?q=Aeneas) is an artificial intelligence model developed by Google DeepMind (introduced in July 2025) designed to contextualize, restore, date, and locate ancient, damaged, or fragmentary Latin inscriptions. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEB6zswFXLHWNUr50PLWgHLrJijQjVr6W2kWxi-0nEWG5P28x4REk6Q6AYXIr_4-SwX6orB160iw-1gZDY6jADE-rMyLIX_CBtabYyxbRp5S5IC0FKOv_i9mUYjCqsIAo3XHp9H8SToS2NFud8WZJzn2TGy17R8ee46ivSWdGGo1sDerU7QQ0ro-Q), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESpQEB6zswFWG8w-mfuRRcY00Tf5VqOjJgOsrTt2K-CqXE-s6eoypHoyZG02a0WBqdldrGAt8XVaVuDbvBZUqmF0wWB67vTLPyOWvvnK21C8H8zGzmP-T2gKM9jIkhbMUAtdjBz2tgHEOzKpNL5Gsd2KzEHZBF7G4G-HU8XdeQU8nJsRShIYoAiQKrhn5lZ9PUkZCdB5kY-CUPYZTuU_Cajx54m8Mw_O8)]
Key Features & Capabilities
   * Training Corpus: Trained on the Latin Epigraphic Dataset (LED), containing over 176,000 inscriptions spanning from 700 BCE to 800 CE across 62 Roman provinces. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEShwEB6zswFY0QjEO1BaHYlLqtOldhTzW34JmzNcjfqspVSxVxQfS3FfCjIgnTyQY5P60-KhG_C1Qo1g5DpaR8Erpqk82hlKq2VHUtZM3Fc3V5Zxh9PU1AeCaIoIcqdeTINbke3PauVzSGcq3rR0qbEwFvqIk3yWWa7H33PE_hEu_MAFtEmru3nFQ), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESagHrOzAVQ74c-Pbfo3bTeRBSUgmirHMhnnPyeg_9ae9efFRc36J65fhdh6268CThg5NIfI__i0y-kutek3mrnJvGLXx8Pt1Q-uNmrtE80n4r_w3XkJmvLw4W9AfPwWYprO7XU9HjQe1QhFo)]
   * Text & Image Input: A multimodal model that processes both weathered stone images and text to identify geographical provenance and shared syntax or formulas. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEShwEB6zswFY0QjEO1BaHYlLqtOldhTzW34JmzNcjfqspVSxVxQfS3FfCjIgnTyQY5P60-KhG_C1Qo1g5DpaR8Erpqk82hlKq2VHUtZM3Fc3V5Zxh9PU1AeCaIoIcqdeTINbke3PauVzSGcq3rR0qbEwFvqIk3yWWa7H33PE_hEu_MAFtEmru3nFQ), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEB6zswFXLHWNUr50PLWgHLrJijQjVr6W2kWxi-0nEWG5P28x4REk6Q6AYXIr_4-SwX6orB160iw-1gZDY6jADE-rMyLIX_CBtabYyxbRp5S5IC0FKOv_i9mUYjCqsIAo3XHp9H8SToS2NFud8WZJzn2TGy17R8ee46ivSWdGGo1sDerU7QQ0ro-Q)]
   * Gap Restoration: Restores missing or broken text segments of arbitrary length, achieving high top-20 accuracy on character sequences. transcript:
The Vesuvius Challenge is a global open science competition that uses artificial intelligence and 3D imaging to read carbonized ancient papyrus scrolls from the Villa of the Papyri in Herculaneum.

What are the Herculaneum Scrolls?

• The Eruption: When Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 CE, it buried a Roman villa in Herculaneum under 20 meters of volcanic ash.
• The Damage: The extreme heat carbonized hundreds of papyrus scrolls, turning them into fragile, blackened blocks that crumble if anyone tries to unroll them.
• The Library: The site preserves an ancient library—believed to have belonged to Lucius Calpurnius Piso Caesoninus, Julius Caesar’s father-in-law—containing lost philosophical works.

How the Technology Works

• 3D CT Scanning: Scanners and particle accelerators map the internal layers of the unopened scrolls in high-resolution 3D.
• Virtual Unwrapping: Software traces and flattens the warped, crushed layers of papyrus digitally.
• AI Ink Detection: Because carbon-based ink has a density very similar to carbonized papyrus under X-rays, machine learning models are trained to spot faint surface texture changes and hidden ink traces invisible to the naked eye.

Major Milestones & Prizes

• Launch: Founded in 2023 by Nat Friedman, Daniel Gross, and computer scientist Brent Seales.
• First Word: Luke Farritor decoded the first Greek word ("purple") in late 2023.
• Full Scroll Unwrapped: Researchers and contestants successfully read PHerc. 1667 (Scroll 4), revealing 22 columns of ancient Greek philosophical text (likely Stoic writing) across more than a meter of charred paper.
• Current Competitions: The project features ongoing monthly awards and a $2 million total pool, including a $1,000,000 Grand Prize targeted for full scroll decipherment.

transcript:
The intersection of artificial intelligence and faith spans ethics, spiritual authority, and technological governance.

The Trust and Authority Shift

• Growing Reliance on AI: Research from organizations like Barna Group shows that many practicing Christians increasingly turn to AI tools for personal domains, including financial stability (61%), general well-being (56%), self-understanding (54%), relationships (53%), and spiritual growth (48%).
• The Spiritual Authority Gap: Roughly 30% to 44% of younger demographics (such as Gen Z and Millennials) feel AI guidance can match that of human pastors, though pastors themselves express low trust (6%–12%) in AI as a spiritual authority.
• Core Anxieties: Practicing Christians cite major concerns regarding scriptural misinterpretation (83%), pastor replacement (72%), replacing God (65%), and losing faith (73%).

Tech Companies Turning to Faith for Ethics

• Moral Alignment Initiatives: Major tech companies (including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft) have actively engaged with religious leaders, scholars, and ethicists from over 15 religious traditions to help inform AI morality and alignment.
• The Consensus Challenge: Studies from the Consortium for Evaluating Faith and Ethics in AI (CEFE-AI)—including a multi-institution consortium involving BYU, Notre Dame, Baylor, and Yeshiva—reveal that general-purpose LLMs systematically omit or gloss over faith and religious context when handling everyday ethical dilemmas (such as grief, marriage, guilt, and depression), while sometimes exhibiting measurable biases toward or against specific traditions.
• Theologians' Critique: Scholars like Noreen Herzfeld note that AI models are not sentient, lack an embodied existence or a soul, and caution against "religion washing" or reducing human identity down to biological algorithms.

Collaborative and Pluralist Frameworks

• AI and Faith: A global nonprofit network of faith leaders, technologists, ethicists, and scholars works to apply ancient religious wisdom to modern AI governance, human dignity, and responsible innovation.
• Interfaith and Academic Dialogues: Programs like Harvard’s Christianity and AI conference and global initiatives explore how traditional anthropologies—views of human creativity, reasoning, and the image of God—hold up in an algorithmic age.
